title: d-Matrix Joins the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion Platform
gist: d-Matrix will scale its Raptor 3D-DRAM inference accelerator using NVIDIA's NVLink Fusion interconnect in MGX racks alongside NVIDIA Vera CPUs, ConnectX-9, BlueField-4 DPUs and Spectrum-X switching — dropping its earlier self-built JetStream Ethernet networking in favor of NVIDIA's rack-scale stack, which lets NVIDIA capture the CPU/networking socket even when a rival's AI chip wins the deployment.

insights.claim: d-Matrix's Raptor 3D-DRAM accelerator for generative inference, showcased at Hot Chips 2026, was one of the most popular pieces at the conference, ranking in ServeTheHome's top 5 from the show.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Strong conference reception for d-Matrix's memory-centric inference architecture signals real technical differentiation and market interest ahead of commercial deployment, worth tracking for design wins.
insights.locator: We covered the d-Matrix Raptor 3D-DRAM Accelerator

insights.claim: d-Matrix's roadmap explicitly plans to scale beyond a single Raptor XPU to multiple XPUs and then to larger clusters, and it will use NVIDIA's NVLink Fusion technology to scale up within NVIDIA MGX racks.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Adopting NVLink Fusion is the concrete mechanism by which d-Matrix moves from single-chip demos to rack-scale deployable inference clusters — a key milestone gating its path to production revenue.
insights.locator: d-Matrix Joins the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion Platform

insights.claim: About a year before this NVLink Fusion deal, d-Matrix had built its own JetStream 400G Ethernet card to demonstrate it could handle data-center-scale AI inference networking itself, rather than relying on a partner's interconnect.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: The shift from a proprietary Ethernet networking card to adopting NVIDIA's NVLink Fusion stack marks a strategic pivot away from self-built networking toward standardized, partner-provided interconnect — a sign that building competitive AI-cluster networking in-house was harder or less attractive than partnering.
insights.locator: About a year ago, we covered the d-Matrix JetStream 400G

insights.claim: d-Matrix's new NVIDIA announcement covers not just NVLink Fusion chiplets but a full adjacent stack: NVIDIA Vera CPUs, ConnectX-9, BlueField-4 DPUs, NVLink switch trays, and Spectrum-X switching.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: d-Matrix is effectively adopting nearly the entire NVIDIA rack-scale reference architecture around its own accelerator chip, meaning its go-to-market bundles NVIDIA silicon across CPU, DPU, and networking rather than just the interconnect fabric.

insights.claim: NVLink Fusion gives d-Matrix a relatively standardized way to scale its accelerators up and out without having to reinvent networking on FPGAs itself.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Removes a major engineering burden (custom networking silicon/FPGA development) and time-to-market risk for a smaller accelerator startup competing against much larger incumbents.
insights.quote: NVLink Fusion gives the company a relatively standardized way to scale up and out without reinventing networking on FPGAs.

insights.claim: Adopting NVIDIA's rack-scale platform gives d-Matrix a deployment model that hyperscalers and neoclouds already understand how to deploy and maintain, easing customer adoption.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Familiarity with the deployment stack lowers integration risk and sales friction for hyperscaler/neocloud customers, which is often the deciding factor for a startup accelerator winning production deployments over a technically similar but operationally unfamiliar alternative.
insights.quote: It also gives the company a rack-scale platform that hyper-scalers and neoclouds understand how to deploy and maintain.

insights.claim: Even if d-Matrix wins customer deployments for its own AI accelerators, NVIDIA still gets to supply the interconnect and CPUs used within that deployment via NVLink Fusion, Vera CPUs, and networking components.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: NVLink Fusion functions as a hedge for NVIDIA: it monetizes rival AI accelerator wins by capturing the surrounding CPU/networking revenue, reducing NVIDIA's downside from losing the accelerator socket itself.
insights.quote: For NVIDIA, even if d-Matrix gets customer wins for its accelerators, NVIDIA gets to provide the interconnect and CPUs found within that deployment.

insights.claim: If d-Matrix wins a deployment using NVIDIA's Vera CPU, that is a CPU socket that AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm do not win, and one that Arm's own AGI CPU effort also does not win.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Highlights a second-order competitive effect: every AI-accelerator design win that bundles NVIDIA's Vera CPU is a lost data-center CPU socket for AMD, Intel, Qualcomm, and even Arm's own reference CPU designs, expanding NVIDIA's server-CPU footprint indirectly through accelerator partnerships.
insights.quote: if d-Matrix wins a deployment, it is a CPU socket that AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm do not win, nor does the Arm AGI CPU.
